recent_posts.title: What developers need to know about AI tools and agents in 2025
recent_posts.summary: A wide-ranging conversation between developer podcast host Chris Jenkins and Henry Garner (CTO at JUX) covering the current AI landscape for software engineers. Topics include the impact of AI coding tools on developer jobs, the MCP vs skills debate, when fine-tuning still makes sense vs using frontier models, neurosymbolic AI and the potential return of Prolog-style symbolic reasoning, multi-agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, Gastown), LLM observability tools like Phoenix and Temporal, and a behavioral specification language called Ali developed at JUX. The conversation emphasizes maintaining engineering judgment and design oversight while delegating implementation to AI agents.

recent_posts.title: Asciinema: Terminal Recording Done Right (with Marcin Kulik)
recent_posts.summary: A deep-dive podcast conversation with Marcin Kulik, creator of asciinema, covering 14 years of development history. The discussion traces the project's evolution from a Python wrapper around Unix's `script` command to a multi-language ecosystem spanning Python, ClojureScript, Go, Rust, and Elixir. Key technical topics include building a proper VT100-compatible terminal emulator (replacing naive regex parsing), the challenges of DOM rendering for terminal playback, why ClojureScript's immutable data structures caused GC pressure at high frame rates, the move to Rust compiled to WebAssembly for the player's core, using Rustler to embed the same Rust terminal emulator library (AVT) in an Elixir/Phoenix backend, and the recent rewrite of the CLI recorder from Python to Rust to support live terminal streaming with reconnection resilience.

recent_posts.title: SpacetimeDB: What launching an MMO can teach us about Databases (with Tyler Cloutier)
recent_posts.summary: SpacetimeDB is a distributed database that runs application logic inside the database itself via WebAssembly. Clients connect directly and receive real-time updates through subscriptions. The architecture uses functional programming principles with reducers that transform database state, enabling features like time-travel debugging and zero-downtime deployments. The team validated the approach by building an MMO (BitCraft Online), encountering performance challenges during launch including hardware issues, unoptimized queries scanning millions of rows, and cascading failures from synchronous logging. The database uses an in-memory relational model compatible with Entity Component Systems, supports TypeScript and React integration, and achieves microsecond-level transaction latencies by colocating logic with data.

recent_posts.title: Rewriting SQLite in Rust with open contributions
recent_posts.summary: Glauber Costa discusses his journey from Linux kernel contributor to co-founding Turso, a complete rewrite of SQLite in Rust. He explains SQLite's limitations, particularly its single-writer concurrency model and closed contribution model, which prevent features like concurrent writes, CDC, and vector search. The rewrite attracted 9,000 GitHub stars and 60 contributors in under a month, demonstrating significant pent-up demand. Costa emphasizes that the primary motivation isn't just technical improvements, but creating an open-contribution community around an embedded database, using deterministic simulation testing to ensure SQLite-level reliability while enabling architectural innovations impossible in a fork.

recent_posts.title: Building agentic AI systems with Google's agent development kit
recent_posts.summary: Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK) is an open-source Python framework for building agentic AI systems that can think and act autonomously. Unlike simple LLM chains, ADK enables complex multi-agent workflows where agents can execute tools, manage memory across sessions, and communicate with each other. The framework includes built-in testing with trajectory validation, observability tooling, and integration with MCP (Model Context Protocol) for tool discovery. Google is also introducing A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol to enable horizontal communication between agents, complementing MCP's vertical agent-to-tool communication. The discussion covers practical considerations like when to use agents versus traditional code, deployment patterns, security guardrails, and debugging strategies including the ADK Web UI for tracing and evaluation.

recent_posts.title: Building Observable Systems with eBPF and Linux (with Mohammed Aboullaite)
recent_posts.summary: eBPF enables continuous profiling of production systems by loading programs into the Linux kernel without recompilation. This approach provides unified monitoring across languages and services with 1-5% overhead, allowing developers to identify performance bottlenecks at the code level in real-time. The technique addresses data volume challenges through time-based aggregation strategies and integrates with distributed tracing to correlate requests across microservices.

recent_posts.title: Solving Git's Pain Points with Jujutsu (with Martin von Zweigbergk)
recent_posts.summary: Martin von Zweigbergk discusses Jujutsu (JJ), a Git-compatible version control system that addresses Git's usability challenges. JJ automatically snapshots the working copy as commits, eliminates the staging area, and stores merge conflicts as algebraic expressions of input trees rather than conflict markers. This enables seamless navigation between commits, simpler rebasing, and the ability to resolve conflicts at your convenience. The tool uses Rust for performance, supports pluggable storage backends, maintains an operation log for granular undo/redo, and aims to eventually support large files and cloud-based repositories for game studios and enterprise users.

recent_posts.title: Getting New Tech Adopted (with Dov Katz)
From Unit Tests to Whole Universe Tests (with Will Wilson)
recent_posts.summary: Property testing can be extended beyond unit tests to entire distributed systems using deterministic hypervisors. Antithesis has built a system that simulates complete virtual environments where all operations are deterministic and reproducible, allowing for comprehensive testing of complex systems. The approach uses time travel capabilities to explore rare bug conditions by building on intermediate states rather than starting from scratch each time. This enables finding bugs that traditional testing misses because they require multiple rare events to occur in sequence.
